context.analysis:
## Overview
This hybrid architecture gradually modernizes a legacy regional insurance claims system by decoupling online submission and adjuster interfaces from an on-premise mainframe. It balances low cloud team experience with strict consistency and performance requirements using managed Azure services and asynchronous integration patterns.

## Key Elements
- Customers & Brokers
- Claims Adjusters
- Finance & Compliance Auditors
- New Claims Platform (Azure West Europe)
- Azure Service Bus
- Enterprise Service Bus / Integration Gateway (On-premise)
- Legacy Mainframe COBOL/DB2 System of Record (On-premise)
- Insurer Active Directory (On-premise)

## Relationships
- Customers & Brokers → New Claims Platform (HTTPS / JSON): Online claim submission
- Claims Adjusters → New Claims Platform (HTTPS / HTML): Web application handling
- New Claims Platform ↔ Azure Service Bus (AMQP / HTTPS): Asynchronous event queuing
- Azure Service Bus ↔ Enterprise Service Bus (IPsec VPN / Azure ExpressRoute, TLS 1.3): Hybrid message transit
- Enterprise Service Bus → Legacy Mainframe (Managed File Transfer / MQ / APIs): Gradual data synchronization
- New Claims Platform → Insurer Active Directory (OIDC / OAuth2 via Entra ID Connect): Single sign-on and MFA

## Technology Stack
- Azure App Service: Container hosting for the New Claims Platform due to low cloud experience and managed PaaS simplicity
- Azure Service Bus: Asynchronous message broker to buffer events and protect against the 23:00-05:00 mainframe batch window
- Azure ExpressRoute / IPsec VPN: Secure hybrid network interconnect with mutual TLS (mTLS)
- OpenTelemetry & Azure Monitor: Distributed tracing and observability to monitor sub-2s adjuster screen performance and zero-loss consistency

## Rationale
The hybrid approach isolates expensive mainframe changes to at most once per quarter while migrating claim types individually. Asynchronous queuing and Azure-hosted UI buffering satisfy performance and consistency requirements without extending the rigid nightly batch window.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a hybrid insurance claims modernization platform that gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe with modern cloud services. Its core purpose is to enable online claim submissions and fast adjuster workflows while maintaining synchronization with the legacy system.]

## Key Elements
- [Customer Portal App (React/TypeScript, Azure Static Web Apps)]
- [Adjuster Web App (React/Node.js BFF)]
- [Claims Core API (.NET Core modular monolith, Azure Container Apps)]
- [Integration Worker (.NET background service, Azure Container Apps)]
- [Audit & Compliance Service (Azure Function)]
- [Claim Read Database (Azure SQL Database)]
- [Azure Service Bus]
- [Enterprise Service Bus / Integration Gateway]
- [Legacy Mainframe COBOL/DB2 System of Record]
- [Insurer Active Directory / Azure Entra ID]

## Relationships
- [Customers & Brokers -> Customer Portal App (HTTPS / JSON)]
- [Claims Adjusters -> Adjuster Web App (HTTPS / HTML)]
- [Customer Portal App & Adjuster Web App -> Claims Core API (HTTPS / JSON)]
- [Claims Core API -> Claim Read Database (TDS / TCP)]
- [Claims Core API -> Azure Service Bus (AMQP)]
- [Integration Worker -> Azure Service Bus (AMQP)]
- [Azure Service Bus -> Enterprise Service Bus / Integration Gateway (IPsec VPN / Azure ExpressRoute, TLS 1.3)]
- [Enterprise Service Bus / Integration Gateway -> Legacy Mainframe COBOL/DB2 System of Record (Managed File Transfer / MQ / APIs)]
- [Customer Portal App & Adjuster Web App -> Insurer Active Directory (OIDC / OAuth2 via Azure Entra ID Connect)]

## Technology Stack
- [Azure Container Apps: Unified hosting for backend services balancing microservice separation with low operational complexity for teams with limited cloud experience.]
- [Azure SQL Database: Provides relational storage with Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) and Private Endpoints for data protection and fast read performance.]
- [Azure Service Bus: Asynchronous messaging to buffer events and handle the nightly mainframe batch window (23:00-05:00).]
- [.NET Core: Backend runtime for core business logic, APIs, and background worker processes.]
- [Azure Key Vault: Secure runtime credential and secret injection using managed identities.]

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture decouples modern web interfaces from the legacy mainframe, satisfying performance requirements via read-side caching despite slow mainframe responses. The container design isolates components to ensure reliable data consistency and modular claim-type rollbacks within the required timeframe.]

Customer Portal App.analysis:
## Overview
Gradually replaces a 30-year-old mainframe claims system with a modern hybrid platform while legacy processing continues. Utilizes Azure cloud services and asynchronous messaging to modernize user interfaces while protecting legacy constraints.

## Key Elements
- Customers & Brokers, Claims Adjusters, Finance & Compliance Auditors
- Customer Portal App (React/TypeScript, Azure Static Web Apps)
- Adjuster Web App (React/Node.js BFF)
- Claims Core API (.NET Core modular monolith, Azure Container Apps)
- Integration Worker (.NET background service, Azure Container Apps)
- Audit & Compliance Service (Azure Function)
- Claim Read Database (Azure SQL Database)
- Azure Service Bus
- Enterprise Service Bus / Integration Gateway
- Legacy Mainframe COBOL/DB2 System of Record
- Insurer Active Directory

## Relationships
- Customers & Brokers -> Customer Portal App [HTTPS / JSON]
- Claims Adjusters -> Adjuster Web App [HTTPS / HTML]
- Customer Portal App -> Claims Core API [HTTPS / JSON]
- Adjuster Web App -> Claims Core API [HTTPS / JSON]
- Claims Core API -> Claim Read Database [TDS / TCP]
- Claims Core API -> Azure Service Bus [AMQP]
- Integration Worker -> Azure Service Bus [AMQP]
- Azure Service Bus -> Enterprise Service Bus / Integration Gateway [IPsec VPN / Azure ExpressRoute, TLS 1.3]
- Enterprise Service Bus / Integration Gateway -> Legacy Mainframe COBOL/DB2 System of Record [Managed File Transfer / MQ / APIs]
- Customer Portal App -> Insurer Active Directory [OIDC / OAuth2 via Azure Entra ID Connect]
- Adjuster Web App -> Insurer Active Directory [OIDC / OAuth2 via Azure Entra ID Connect]

## Technology Stack
- Azure Static Web Apps: Hosts SPAs with global CDN distribution and minimal operational overhead.
- Azure Container Apps: Runs .NET Core microservices without complex infrastructure management.
- Azure SQL Database: Stores read models to isolate frontend traffic from mainframe latency.
- Azure Service Bus: Asynchronously buffers events to protect against the rigid nightly mainframe batch window.
- Azure Entra ID Connect: Delivers secure single sign-on integrating with on-premise Active Directory.

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates expensive mainframe dependencies behind asynchronous queues and read models, ensuring high performance for users. It enables incremental, low-risk claim type migration while strictly preserving data consistency and supporting teams with limited cloud experience.

Adjuster Web App.analysis:
## Overview
The New Claims Platform is a hybrid cloud solution gradually replacing a 30-year-old on-premise COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims system. It enables online claim submission for customers and modern claims processing for adjusters via managed Azure services while maintaining core data integrity.

## Key Elements
- Claims Adjusters (person)
- Adjuster Web App (container: React/Node.js BFF)
- UI Shell & Routing (component)
- Claim Action Queue (component)
- BFF Orchestrator Service / BFF Claim Controller (component)
- Session & Token Manager (component)
- Claims Core API (container: .NET Core modular monolith, Azure Container Apps)
- Insurer Active Directory (externalSystem)

## Relationships
- Claims Adjuster -> UI Shell & Routing [HTTPS / HTML]
- UI Shell & Routing -> BFF Orchestrator Service [HTTP / JSON]
- BFF Orchestrator Service -> Claims Core API [HTTPS / JSON]
- Session & Token Manager -> Insurer Active Directory [OIDC / OAuth2 via Azure Entra ID Connect]

## Technology Stack
- React / TypeScript: Chosen for the SPA frontend to deliver sub-2-second adjuster screen loads.
- Node.js / Express: Implements the Backend-For-Frontend (BFF) pattern to isolate frontend from backend latency.
- Azure Container Apps: Simplifies deployment and KEDA auto-scaling for teams with low cloud experience.
- Zod / Joi: Used within the BFF for strict JSON payload validation and security hardening.

## Rationale
The hybrid architecture and BFF pattern protect operational stability by isolating legacy mainframe latency and supporting gradual, claim-type-by-claim-type migration. Unified Azure deployment minimizes operational complexity for a team with limited cloud expertise.

Claims Core API.analysis:
## Overview
[The Claims Core API is a modular monolith built on .NET Core and Azure Container Apps that orchestrates claim submissions and routing during a hybrid mainframe modernization. It securely bridges modern cloud interfaces with legacy on-premise systems while ensuring zero claim loss and sub-2-second response times.]

## Key Elements
- Claims Core API (.NET Core modular monolith, Azure Container Apps)
- Claim Submission Component (.NET Core)
- Claim Query & Routing Component (.NET Core)
- Fallback Orchestrator Component (.NET Core)
- Claim Admin & Metadata Component (.NET Core)
- Azure Service Bus (AMQP)
- Claim Read Database (Azure SQL Database)
- Insurer Active Directory (Azure Entra ID Connect)

## Relationships
- Customer Portal App -> Claims Core API: Sends claim submissions [HTTPS / JSON]
- Adjuster Web App -> Claims Core API: Fetches and updates claim data [HTTPS / JSON]
- Claim Submission Component -> Azure Service Bus: Publishes new claim events [AMQP]
- Claim Query & Routing Component -> Claim Read Database: Fetches optimized read models [TDS / TCP]
- Claims Core API -> Insurer Active Directory: Authenticates requests [OIDC / OAuth2 via Entra ID Connect]

## Technology Stack
- .NET Core: Selected for building the modular monolith and internal components due to robust enterprise features and strong typing.
- Azure Container Apps: Chosen to host the API containers, providing managed serverless scaling and built-in health probes for a team with limited cloud experience.
- Azure SQL Database: Utilized for the Claim Read Database to deliver sub-2-second query performance via optimized read models.
- Azure Service Bus: Deployed as an asynchronous message broker to decouple online submissions from mainframe latency using AMQP.
- OpenTelemetry & Polly: Implemented for distributed tracing and circuit breaking to ensure resilience across the hybrid cloud-mainframe boundary.

## Rationale
[This architecture successfully isolates legacy mainframe bottlenecks through asynchronous messaging and feature-flagged routing within a modular monolith. It meets all stringent performance, security, and maintainability requirements while accommodating the team's limited cloud experience.]

Integration Worker.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a hybrid insurance claims modernization platform that gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe with modern cloud services while maintaining legacy data sync. Its core purpose is to decouple online claim submissions and adjuster web applications from the mainframe using Azure services and asynchronous integration patterns.]

## Key Elements
- New Claims Platform
- Customers & Brokers
- Claims Adjusters
- Finance & Compliance Auditors
- Customer Portal App (React/TypeScript, Azure Static Web Apps)
- Adjuster Web App (React/Node.js BFF)
- Claims Core API (.NET Core modular monolith, Azure Container Apps)
- Integration Worker (.NET background service, Azure Container Apps)
- Audit & Compliance Service (Azure Function)
- Claim Read Database (Azure SQL Database)
- Azure Service Bus
- Enterprise Service Bus / Integration Gateway
- Legacy Mainframe COBOL/DB2 System of Record
- Insurer Active Directory

## Relationships
- Customers & Brokers -> Customer Portal App (HTTPS / JSON)
- Claims Adjusters -> Adjuster Web App (HTTPS / HTML)
- Customer Portal App -> Claims Core API (HTTPS / JSON)
- Adjuster Web App -> Claims Core API (HTTPS / JSON)
- Claims Core API -> Claim Read Database (TDS / TCP)
- Claims Core API -> Azure Service Bus (AMQP)
- Integration Worker -> Azure Service Bus (AMQP)
- Azure Service Bus -> Enterprise Service Bus / Integration Gateway (IPsec VPN / Azure ExpressRoute, TLS 1.3)
- Enterprise Service Bus / Integration Gateway -> Legacy Mainframe COBOL/DB2 System of Record (Managed File Transfer / MQ / APIs)
- Customer Portal App -> Insurer Active Directory (OIDC / OAuth2 via Azure Entra ID Connect)
- Adjuster Web App -> Insurer Active Directory (OIDC / OAuth2 via Azure Entra ID Connect)

## Technology Stack
- Azure Static Web Apps: Hosts React/TypeScript frontend with minimal cloud complexity
- Azure Container Apps: Runs containerized modular monoliths and background workers with KEDA scaling
- Azure SQL Database: Provides relational storage for claim read models and idempotency tracking
- Azure Service Bus: Asynchronous event queue using AMQP to buffer messages and protect legacy batch windows
- OpenTelemetry: Distributed tracing across cloud and on-premise hybrid boundaries
- Azure Entra ID: Manages SSO, MFA, and managed identities for secure service-to-service authentication

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture isolates expensive mainframe dependencies behind an asynchronous Azure Service Bus queue, satisfying strict batch-window constraints and ensuring zero data loss. It allows gradual, risk-mitigated claim type migration with a one-day fallback capability while supporting a team with limited cloud experience.]
Integration Worker.yaml_definition:
level: component
scope: "Component diagram for the Integration Worker container"
parentContainer:
  name: "Integration Worker"
elements:
  - type: "component"
    name: "Service Bus Message Listener"
    technology: ".NET background service, Azure Service Bus SDK"
    description: "Listens for asynchronous events from Azure Service Bus to process background integration tasks."
  - type: "component"
    name: "Mainframe Integration Processor"
    technology: ".NET Core"
    description: "Transforms and dispatches integration payloads toward the enterprise integration gateway and legacy systems."
relationships:
  - source: "Service Bus Message Listener"
    destination: "Mainframe Integration Processor"
    description: "Forwards received messages for processing"

Audit & Compliance Service.analysis:
## Overview
[The Insurance Claims Modernization system gradually replaces a 30-year-old on-premise mainframe with a secure hybrid cloud platform in Azure West Europe. It ensures non-repudiation, strict regulatory compliance, and immutable audit trails across legacy and modern workflows.]

## Key Elements
- Finance & Compliance Auditors [person]
- Audit & Compliance Service [container, Azure Function]
- Audit Event Consumer [.NET Isolated Azure Function Trigger]
- Compliance Rules Engine [C# Domain Component]
- Audit Query API [ASP.NET Core Functions HTTP Trigger]
- Compliance Report Generator [.NET Timer Trigger Azure Function]
- Audit Data Store [Azure SQL Database Ledger with Read Replica]
- Azure Service Bus [externalSystem]
- Insurer Active Directory [externalSystem]
- Azure Monitor / Application Insights [externalSystem]

## Relationships
- Finance & Compliance Auditors -> Audit Query API (HTTPS / JSON, Role-Based Access Control)
- Audit Event Consumer -> Azure Service Bus (AMQP)
- Audit Event Consumer -> Audit Data Store (TDS / TCP via Entity Framework Core)
- Compliance Rules Engine -> Audit Data Store (TDS / TCP via Entity Framework Core)
- Compliance Report Generator -> Audit Data Store Ledger Read Replica (TDS / TCP)
- Audit Query API -> Audit Data Store Ledger Read Replica (TDS / TCP)
- Audit & Compliance Service -> Insurer Active Directory (OIDC / OAuth2 via Azure Entra ID, Azure Managed Identity)
- Audit & Compliance Service -> Azure Monitor / Application Insights (HTTPS)

## Technology Stack
- Azure Functions (.NET Isolated): Serverless execution model aligning with team's managed-service preference.
- Azure SQL Database Ledger: Tamper-evident, cryptographically secure append-only audit tables using familiar relational tooling to reduce operational overhead.
- Azure Entra ID & Managed Identities: Secure single sign-on and secret-free authentication.
- Entity Framework Core: Standardized relational data access with read-replica connection routing.

## Rationale
[This architecture fits requirements by establishing tamper-evident, automated compliance tracking using managed Azure components that simplify auditing for regional regulators. Using SQL Ledger and read replicas prevents performance degradation while securing hybrid data consistency under strict migration constraints.]

Claim Read Database.analysis:
## Overview
- Gradually modernizes a regional insurer's legacy mainframe by decoupling online submission and adjuster interfaces using managed Azure services and asynchronous integration patterns.
- Replaces the 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 system over a three-year period while maintaining operational continuity, data consistency, and strict security compliance.

## Key Elements
- Customers & Brokers
- Claims Adjusters
- Finance & Compliance Auditors
- Customer Portal App (React/TypeScript, Azure Static Web Apps)
- Adjuster Web App (React/Node.js BFF)
- Claims Core API (.NET Core modular monolith, Azure Container Apps)
- Integration Worker (.NET background service, Azure Container Apps)
- Audit & Compliance Service (Azure Function)
- Claim Read Database (Azure SQL Database)
- Azure Service Bus
- Enterprise Service Bus / Integration Gateway
- Legacy Mainframe COBOL/DB2 System of Record
- Insurer Active Directory

## Relationships
- Customers & Brokers -> Customer Portal App (HTTPS / JSON)
- Claims Adjusters -> Adjuster Web App (HTTPS / HTML)
- Customer Portal App -> Claims Core API (HTTPS / JSON)
- Adjuster Web App -> Claims Core API (HTTPS / JSON)
- Claims Core API -> Claim Read Database (TDS / TCP)
- Claims Core API -> Azure Service Bus (AMQP)
- Integration Worker -> Azure Service Bus (AMQP)
- Azure Service Bus -> Enterprise Service Bus / Integration Gateway (IPsec VPN / Azure ExpressRoute, TLS 1.3)
- Enterprise Service Bus / Integration Gateway -> Legacy Mainframe COBOL/DB2 System of Record (Managed File Transfer / MQ / APIs)
- Customer Portal App -> Insurer Active Directory (OIDC / OAuth2 via Azure Entra ID Connect)
- Adjuster Web App -> Insurer Active Directory (OIDC / OAuth2 via Azure Entra ID Connect)

## Technology Stack
- Azure Static Web Apps: Hosts React/TypeScript frontend for customers and brokers.
- Azure Container Apps: Runs containerized .NET Core APIs and background integration workers.
- Azure SQL Database: Provides relational read storage with encryption, private endpoints, and Dynamic Data Masking.
- Azure Service Bus: Buffers asynchronous event messaging to protect the mainframe batch window.
- Azure Active Directory (Entra ID Connect): Delivers single sign-on and MFA.

## Rationale
- Hybrid cloud architecture allows the legacy mainframe to remain the system of record while incrementally migrating claim types.
- Managed Azure services minimize operational overhead for a team with limited cloud experience while meeting strict sub-2-second performance and security constraints.
